hypothesis: Pointwise curvature is a per-point robust geometry operator, whereas the current parent R02 uses aggregate geometry (actual_parent_factor_value='aggregate'). At L109 the two typed slots are chemically distinct and locally constrained: slot 12 is a native aromatic C (degree 2, neighbors 18/21, native_to_desired C->C, best donor A:ASP:175:N with strength ~1.5e-06, i.e. no donor contact), and slot 22 is a native aromatic N (degree 2, neighbors 6/13, native_to_desired N->N, anchored to A:VAL:116:N with teacher_match_strength 0.951). Because slot 22 carries a strong directional donor anchor while slot 12 carries none, a pointwise curvature treatment should act differentially across the patch rather than uniformly, and could therefore change the measured spatial force direction/dose at the anchored N22 site relative to the aggregate-geometry parent. The claim under test is that this differential treatment improves local compatibility at L109.
